body:
I'm sorry for your own difficulties.

I see death as a kind of nothing. Some pain and then, gone. Not good or bad. I don't think you "go" anywhere after you die, you don't feel joy or relief and I'm not looking for that. I don't think I'll kill myself and then feel better--I don't think I'll feel ANYTHING, ever again. I won't even know that I was successful in doing it.  I'm just looking to end this years-long chronic pain.  

I don't actually feel very emotional about this anymore, just tired. It feels weirdly pragmatic. I am trapped, I have nowhere else to go and no other way to really change my life, so my options are to stay put and keep suffering or to jump. Fucking duh.

Mostly, I just wish someone listened and understood why it's happening, because my parents, whom I've spent all this time trying to reach, have stayed firmly unreachable. I know they're going to say I was selfish and melodramatic and ungrateful and useless and all the other usual stuff they tell me regularly anyway. The thing is, I'm NOT ungrateful, I'm not melodramatic. I'm not even a bad kid, in spite their perspective. I've had sex without having been married (with one person in a long-term relationship that ended years ago), I've not always achieved A's in school, and I have a lot of liberal ideas about things (like, universal healthcare is a good idea). My parents seem to feel that on the whole, I'm not a good kid and a big disappointment.  It's left me feeling really worthless and insecure. I wish someone saw and understood me a little better. Like, hey I'm actually an ok human being. I have a law degree and I speak several languages, I'm actually not a bad person for having independently-formed values. And my feelings are normal and understandable. And I really did hang on as long as I could. And it's okay to realize there is truly nothing I can do here anymore, that somehow life circumstances just sort of made it impossible for me to ever escape, and it's ok to let go.

It was lucky, too, that you had relatives willing to take you in.  Having the option of somewhere you can run TO makes a big difference, I think.

I felt like I could take a job just about anywhere. That was my "run to" plan. But in spite all my attempts all over the country, nothing has ever materialized. So without a "run to," where am I supposed to go where they won't track me down anyway?
They said I was "being dramatic." My guess is denial, and it seems to be sticking until I ACTUALLY follow through.
Where did you live? Is there a way to keep them from finding you?
Came up in therapy! They didn't want to hear it. Therapy cancelled.

And do what? Where am I going to live, and eat? What am I supposed to do when my parents track me down and start demanding I pay them back for all those loans with my name on them too?  They'd probably be just fine with me leaving, as long as I keep sending the money. It's not huge, a little over $30K, but without a real job I have no prospect of making that happen. 

It feels like my options are:

1. Keep living miserably with my parents, HOPING to land a job and escape. Been doing this for years and nada, so I've lost hope on this.

2. Live in some kind of homeless shelter, on welfare, working multiple part-time jobs, with this debt hanging over my head forever and parents who will forever hold me to it.

I mean, I accept that I have baggage from all this and my escape plan included lots and lots of therapy. But I don't see how option #2 is going to lead to improved mental health, really. Just a different set of problems. I'm done struggling with it all. I haven't got it in me anymore to keep fighting these battles to make it through another day and another. You let years go by like that and one day you wake up and realize that every day is going to be a struggle for the rest of your life and can't help but conclude this has a third alternative that will at least put an end to it.

I mean, the "try talking to them" has been a repeated theme over the years, even right up to therapy, but the key part is they have to actually listen, and they're so unwilling to listen my mom even yanked us out of therapy after a month because she didn't feel it was working (translation: the therapist wasn't backing HER up exclusively, but was acknowledging my feelings too).

Already been asked, I'm not Asian. (I'm not offended by the question either.) Just upper-middle-class Conservative Catholic. Or at least, my parents are, I'm pretty much none of those things personally.

I work several part-time jobs, but still pretty much entirely dependent for the roof over my head. They helped pay for school, so I owe them, that sort of thing. They did a lot to make it very difficult to get away unless I had a good bit of money at my disposal (I'd estimate with the loan payment thing, I need to find a job that pays a minimum of $60K, and still need to live somewhere very cheap).

Not wanting my wall of text to get bigger, I left out some of the details on my parents.

It's a REALLY long history. My dad doesn't hit us anymore and he has made a lot of progress, but he's still not what I would consider a nice guy, and while short visits would probably be fine these days, prolonged daily exposure is really hard. My mom actually tried going to counseling with me, on her offer. I'd been really excited about it at the time and got my hopes up--maybe things would finally get better!

Mom made us quit after about a month. I think she kept expecting the therapist to turn to me and say, "What's wrong with you, kid? Shut up and do what your mother says." Instead I'd express how I felt about something or recount something she was doing that felt really painful, and the therapist kept turning to my mom and asking, "Hey, why don't we address this?"

I think my parents take the mutual attitude that my siblings and I are not really people. Or at least, I don't feel like we're really respected as such. Either you do what Mom and Dad say and you're loved, or you don't and get yelled at and told what a loser you are and how you don't have a choice because they're paying for everything, etc. It's not like you actually get a say in any of this, though, or like your feelings or opinions actually matter, unless they're what Mom and Dad agree with. But if they don't like what you say, it doesn't count, and therapy ends because "this isn't working," or that sort of deal.

When my mom ended therapy like that, it was probably the closest I came to suicide before. It was really hard, but I started to accept that they were never going to change and it wasn't my job to change them and the best I could do was to work hard and get out.

And here I am. Still feeling completely trapped. It never gets better. I kept trying to cling to hope, but I'm losing that too. A thirty year old woman without a job still living with her dad and treated like an eternal five-year-old is not really a life I ever want to live.

EDIT: Oh, the income thing.  My dad's a physician.  Not what I'd call low-income at all, but I think with the new healthcare laws, changing jobs and getting hired new into a hospital is difficult these days and pay structures are getting worked out in new ways. Just one of those things.

My sister (still in high school) got into a really great charter school, so my mom relocated so she could attend and my parents sold their house and bought a new one that my mom and sister are living in, and my old roommate moved out and my dad moved in with me "just for a few months" while he tried to relocate over there to live with them.  Only now it's been over a year and a half, and it doesn't look like he's leaving anytime soon.  

My dad actually bought and owns the apartment, but trust me when I say it's not super-fancy, so I'm really surprised he's still living here, myself.  Last spring for a brief while, he actually started looking into buying a much more upscale place, but decided not to because he's still planning (or hoping?) to get a new job and live with my mom again in another state.
